cells.tense: You are standing here with what has grown, hands on it, knowing what it took to get this far.
cells.ask: Name one thing you've grown — out loud or on paper — and say what it cost you. Both hands on it for a moment, then leave it where it sits. Today, alone, enough.
cells.core:
Something in front of you is working. Not everything in reach is blooming, but one thing grew because you kept showing up, and you know which one. There's no strain in how you hold it — you water it, step back, come back. Steady, and shaped by your own hours.

It got to full size because you carried it from a small idea to a real, finished thing — you chose the yes and the no that made room for it. Name that to yourself instead of only counting what you have. Then let it be finished rather than perfect. Tending without pushing, stepping back without wandering off: you've found where those two meet, and that's the spot to keep standing in. It isn't luck and it isn't a trait. It's a set of decisions you can make again.

cells.verb: Carrying what began as possibility to full form, delivering the finished thing into the world

cells.tense: You are braced for what this thing will need next, already ahead of it, already steering it.
cells.ask: Ten minutes: sit with the growing thing and do nothing to it. No fixing, no planning, no checking elsewhere. If a thought about what it needs arrives, write it down and stay seated.
cells.core:
You are leaning into what comes next before it has arrived. Some part of you is sure that without steady steering it will go wrong, so the checking has thickened — adjusting, planning, pre-solving a future you cannot see yet. That pushing is stronger than what the thing in front of you actually asks for.

Push ahead of something still growing and the looking stops. What shows up is the fear, not the plant. Look at what is here right now without reaching for it — one moment, not forever. That plain looking is where clear sight starts: no verdict, just what is actually present. It isn't quitting, and it isn't neglect. It's standing close enough to work with what's really there instead of what you dread.

cells.tense: Something grew past you, and you stood at the edge of the room without putting a hand on it.
cells.ask: Plant one small thing today — a seed, a bulb, a line in a notebook, a plan on paper — and water it once. Then leave it alone until tomorrow.
cells.core:
There is something that started small and became real, and when it was ready you did not reach for it. Maybe it didn't feel like yours, or the day was already too full. Either way, what it grew into finished without your hand on it, and the gap has been sitting there quietly since.

Closing it isn't a leap and doesn't require feeling ready. Put something in the ground and be a beginning again rather than a manager of results. It will grow without consulting you. Your one job is to show up once a day — no forcing, no vanishing. Being present while it grows is the whole of it, and that is a pace you can actually keep.

cells.tense: You are already tending this — the pen has been in your hand the whole time.
cells.ask: Write one sentence — 'this was my choice because' — and finish it. Read it once, then keep it or throw it away.
cells.core:
You are already the one doing the caring here — the early mornings, the room made, the things you set down so this could keep going. None of it is named as a decision. It reads as something that simply happened, or as keeping up.

When the deciding stays unnamed, the load arrives and the credit doesn't. Writing one sentence saying the choice was yours is not a medal. It's a small correction to the record. The no's and yes's were made by someone, and that someone is available to be found. Nothing has to change about the work. But a thing tended by someone aware becomes easier to stand beside, and the weight of it can be set down in turns instead of carried all at once.
